lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon \u003cb\u003eΔH ≈:
"

With ΔH ≈ −168 kJ/mol and ΔS ≈ −148 J/(mol·K) (freedom is lost when two molecules join into one), ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is very negative at room temperature. But at high temperatures the −TΔS term gains weight until ΔG = 0 (≈ 1135 K under standard conditions): the retro-Diels–Alder becomes favorable and is a way to generate dienes (e.g. cracking of cyclopentadiene from its dimer).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la Diels–Alder de:
"

In the normal-demand Diels–Alder the dominant interaction is HOMO(diene)–LUMO(dienophile). An electron-withdrawing group on the dienophile (C=O, C≡N, NO₂) lowers the LUMO and reduces the gap, and a donor group on the diene (OR, alkyl) raises the HOMO. Compare in “Graphs”: ethene barely reacts; with propenal or propenenitrile the reaction is much easier.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ereacc:
"

The Diels–Alder reaction forms a six-membered ring from a conjugated diene (4 π electrons) and a dienophile (2 π electrons): a [4+2] cycloaddition. The diene only reacts in the s-cis conformation (the two ends of the diene facing each other, at ≈ 3 Å); in the more stable s-trans, the ends are far apart. Rotation about the C2–C3 bond (≈ 16 kJ/mol barrier) is fast at room temperature.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa reacción es \u003c:
"

The reaction is concerted and synchronous: in a single cyclic transition state the two C–C σ bonds form, the C1=C2 double bond and that of the dienophile become single, and a new C=C between C2 and C3 appears. The approach is suprafacial: the dienophile approaches one face of the diene. 2 π bonds break and 2 σ bonds form: ΔH ≈ −168 kJ/mol (butadiene + ethene → cyclohexene).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa reacción está perm:
"

The reaction is allowed by orbital symmetry: the HOMO of the diene (ψ₂) and the LUMO of the dienophile (π*) have the same phase at the two pairs of atoms that bond (C1···Ca and C4···Cb): constructive overlap at both ends. The blue and red lobes indicate the phases. HOMO(dienophile)–LUMO(diene) overlap would also be possible, but with a larger energy gap.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eSi el sustituyente de:
"

If the dienophile substituent is placed under the diene (endo) or away (exo), different stereoisomers are obtained. In most cases the kinetic product is the endo, due to secondary orbital interactions between the π system of the substituent (C=O) and carbons C2 and C3 of the diene. The exo is usually more stable thermodynamically because of less steric hindrance.

"
